key_insight: A backward-mapping, genome-guided workflow can translate device-level targets into interpretable chemical rules to discover stable, lead-free double perovskites.
engineering_relevance: The framework enables faster inverse design of Pb-free halide semiconductors by narrowing 13,088 compositions to a small set of DFT-validated candidates with desirable stability and optoelectronic properties.
method: Filter charge-balanced A2BB'X6 candidates with halide-aware geometric formability rules.
Encode six families of chemical-genome descriptors and train evolutionary-optimized ML surrogates for stability and band gap prediction.
Use SHAP interpretation plus DFT phenotype closure to validate final candidates and extract design rules.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports screening 13,088 compositions and validating seven final candidates with DFT for structure, band edges, effective masses, dielectric response, optics, conductivity, reflectivity, energy-loss spectra, and XRD fingerprints.
watch_item: Model-driven selection depends on the quality of surrogate labels and DFT approximations, so transferability beyond the screened halide double-perovskite space may be limited.
paper_title: Backward Mapping from Device Targets to Chemical Genomes for Interpretable Discovery of Phase-Stable Lead-Free Double Perovskites with DFT-Validated Design Rules
